subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
outcomes: Find key words that show a question asks for agreement, a suggestion or feelings.
Put adverbs of frequency and time phrases in the right place.
Describe how a city makes me feel.

tf.s: The question 'What do they both think?' asks for agreement.
'What advice does Henry give?' asks about feelings.
tf.why: Advice is a suggestion, not a feeling.

tf.s: Speakers often say the same idea in different words.
tf.why: Yes, so listen for meaning, not only the same words.

tf.s: Adverbs of frequency usually go after the verb be.
tf.why: Like 'I am always tired on Thursday evenings.'

tf.s: Adverbs of frequency usually go after main verbs.
tf.why: They go before main verbs: 'I usually stay up late.'

tf.s: Time phrases like 'once a week' usually go at the end of a sentence.
tf.why: Yes: 'Tom and I go skating once a week.'

tf.s: 'Hardly ever' has a similar meaning to 'rarely'.
Before you listen, it helps to underline key words in the questions.
tf.why: Key words help you know what to listen for.
They are opposites: stressed means worried, relaxed means calm.

boxes.q: Which word shows that a question asks for a suggestion?
boxes.why: 'Should' is used for advice and suggestions.

o: How does Dylan feel about his new city?
I am always tired on Thursday evenings.
I always am tired on Thursday evenings.
I am tired always on Thursday evenings.

boxes.q: Where do time phrases usually go?
boxes.why: Time phrases usually go at the end of the sentence.

boxes.q: Which one is a time phrase?
boxes.why: 'Once a month' is a time phrase; the others are adverbs.

boxes.q: Which word means 'calm and not worried'?
How does Dylan feel about his new city?
boxes.why: He is surprised by how friendly people are.

boxes.q: Order: usually / it / dark / isn't / in June
o: It isn't usually dark in June.
It isn't dark in usually June.
It dark isn't usually in June.
boxes.why: After be, the adverb comes next: isn't usually.

boxes.q: What do the two friends in conversation 3 agree about?
boxes.why: They both enjoy the different seasons.

hunt.q: Adverbs of frequency go ___ main verbs.

mcq.q: What should you do before you listen?
o: Underline key words in the questions
mcq.why: Key words help you focus while you listen.

mcq.q: 'You will hear two friends. What do they both think?' This question asks for…
Which of these is a time phrase?
mcq.why: 'Now and then' is a time phrase.

mcq.q: Rewrite: My parents go to the cinema. (hardly ever)
o: My parents hardly ever go to the cinema.
My parents go hardly ever to the cinema.
Hardly ever my parents go to the cinema.
My parents go to hardly ever the cinema.
mcq.why: The adverb goes before the main verb 'go'.

mcq.q: Correct this sentence: 'Tom and I go once a week skating.'
o: Tom and I go skating once a week.
Tom and I go a once week skating.
Tom once and I go skating a week.
Tom and I skating go once a week.
mcq.why: The time phrase goes at the end.

o: I usually study in the evening.
I study usually in the evening.
I am study usually in the evening.
I usually am study in the evening.

mcq.q: One friend laughs more in the country. The other worries more in the city. What do they agree about?
o: They are both more stressed in the city.
They both want to visit the country less.
They are both relaxed in the city.
mcq.why: Both ideas show the city makes them more stressed.

mcq.q: Speaker A: 'It had amazing history.' Speaker B: 'Yes, it was quite an interesting documentary.' What does this show?
o: They say the same idea in different words.
mcq.why: Listen for the same idea, even when the words change.

mcq.q: Why does 'always' come after 'am' in 'I am always tired'?
o: Adverbs of frequency go after the verb be.
Adverbs always go at the end.
mcq.why: With be, the adverb comes after the verb.
